findings.area: L3/L6 + M1 coupling: authority matrix vs actual writers
findings.summary: authority-matrix.json types 'ALL writer procedures' per table and sets allOnlineDirectAuthorityDML INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE=false, but it is not reconciled with the 72028 writers that the census itself records for those tables. Unmapped product writers: inv.nodes runtime fail-closed quarantine build_execution.py:304 _mark_node_quarantined and node_transport.py:247 _quarantine_gpu_node; inv.node_channels node_channels.py:183 provision_channel INSERT and :218 revoke_channel UPDATE (matrix: b_member_cas only); inv.evidence five plain INSERTs (build_execution.py:666, results.py:219, runs.py:180, shard_completion.py:142, storage_commit.py:327) vs single writer b_commit_business_nonce_evidence; public.nodes ORM enroll_node INSERT (services/nodes.py:113), mark_lost_nodes status='lost' (:329), retirement/certificate binding that NodePrincipal.lock_current checks (status 'retired', certificate_fingerprint) vs matrix runtime heartbeat columns only; public.storage_contributions create (storage.py:76) and revoke status/revoked_at (:126-127) vs OP UPDATE without INSERT/revoked_at. inv.nodes.status is writable by both the online verifier (b_commit_node_observation) and containment (b_change_node_containment), and public.nodes.status by sv_b_runtime, with no one-way transition rule (72028 observation only does offline->online / online->offline). As written, either the plain paths run as sv_b_runtime and these writers fail (a permission-denied quarantine aborts instead of quarantining), or a legacy online pool keeps direct DML on B authority tables, which bypasses allOnlineDirectAuthorityDML=false and the SD lock order. 'Plain external behavior preserved' and the typed matrix cannot both hold.
findings.revision: For every census writer record (SQL and ORM) on a matrix table, name the B procedure, principal, columns and allowed status transitions (e.g. a runtime one-way QUARANTINE-only procedure; observation may only toggle online/offline and never clear quarantined/draining/retired), or retire it explicitly with its replacement. State which pool runs plain paths and that it has no direct DML on these tables. Add a causal census<->matrix check where an unmapped writer or a removed mapping fails. Static/docs only; actual PG grants stay future.

The reached functions' helperEdges are incomplete, e.g. placement.reserve:130 _admit_locked (lock_run + require_execution). (c) canonicalBPlan, outerTransaction and requiredBPlan are one constant string each across 343 plans / 2933 records. Probe A1: append A1 (renew, prior=A0), then revoke A0, then pause/invalidate/ARM: commit_activation(A1) returns True. The contract says explicit revocation blocks the lane, but whether revoking A_k revokes descendants appended from it is unstated.

findings.area: M3 gate state machine and lost ack
findings.summary: The Node gate is not monotonic. Probe A4: after a completed switch to g1, a freshly signed INVALIDATE g1 plus ARM of the old release g0 is accepted and acknowledged. Probe A5: after a restart, an ARM naming an old-generation release is acknowledged, because ARM checks command.generation but not release.generation. Business stays denied: the receipt binds gateAckHash (A4b), node_accepts checks generation and the CP pointer CAS refuses (A4c). But 'acknowledged invalidation' is not terminal. Separately, a lost or stale (>60s) ARM ack leaves the Node ARMED with no current pointer. A repeat ARM is refused (A3b), and no Node read path is specified that re-emits the durable record and ack ('lost ack requires exact Node record/proof' has no artifact).
findings.revision: Make INVALIDATED gate IDs and releases terminal at the Node, and require release.generation == current generation at ARM. Define the observe-lane read of the latest durable gate record and ack, plus stale-ack recovery (invalidate, then a fresh gateId) or B-RECOVERY1.

findings.summary: DELIVERY_CHALLENGE and KEY_DELIVERY_RECEIPT are signed by OPERATOR_RELEASE, the same anchor as APPROVAL/RELEASE/DELEGATION/GATE_CONTROL. The postcommit sv_b_delivery_controller has no DB approval EXECUTE, but nothing states that its signing access is restricted to these two purposes. Root asked for 'its own protected delivery-receipt signature' outside runtime/use-issuer custody.
findings.revision: Either a distinct key-delivery-receipt key in the Node trust configuration, or an explicit caller->purpose allowlist in the operator signing service (controller: KEY_DELIVERY_PREPARE and KEY_DELIVERY_RECEIPT only), with a negative fixture.
